title: A strategy for debugging
recap: Useful debugging starts with reliable reproduction. Fixed inputs and precise expected checkpoints make repeated observations comparable and prevent the investigation from drifting.

Runtime checkpoints can divide an execution path into regions. A correct checkpoint moves the search later, while an incorrect checkpoint proves the cause occurred earlier, allowing the search to home in efficiently.
objectives: Follow precise reproduction steps with deterministic inputs.
Choose an initial checkpoint near the middle of a calculation pipeline.
Use correct and incorrect observations to discard parts of the execution path.
Stop when one stage has correct inputs but produces an incorrect output.
warnings: A failure that cannot be reproduced consistently provides weak diagnostic evidence.
The final incorrect value only proves that the cause occurred somewhere earlier in its executed path.
Reading every line from the beginning is less efficient than selecting informative checkpoints.
Do not edit while gathering baseline observations, because changed code invalidates the comparison.
challenge: Isolate and repair the sensor pipeline fault. Raw reading 18 with offset 2 must normalize to 20; scaling by 3 must produce 60; combining a second-zone reading of 12 must produce 72; and holding back 7 units must leave 65. Run the untouched starter first. Break after combineZones() as a midpoint checkpoint. If that value is wrong, move earlier; if it is correct, move later. Compare normalized and scaled values until one stage has correct inputs but an incorrect result. Repair only that stage and rerun the complete fixed-input reproduction. Preserve the four-stage module and calculate every displayed value.
hints: Use combined as the first checkpoint. If it is not 72, inspect normalized and scaled rather than starting at the final reserve calculation.
When normalized is 20, inspect the value returned from scaleReading() and compare it with the expected intermediate value 60.
A scale factor of 3 means the incoming normalized reading contributes three equal times to the scaled result.
